Your three weapons

Voting Arrows

Precision strikes. Every registered, informed ballot aimed at the exact lever of power — a race, a funding bill, a check on power — instead of sprayed into the void.

Axe of Freedom

Heavy swings that cut red tape and bad arguments: asking who built this crisis, who profits, and where's the proof? before anyone spends your future on it.

Sword of Youth

The long game. Young voters are the largest bloc that mostly stays home in midterms — which is exactly why The Fade fears you showing up, every cycle, in force.

Why we march — home is the quest

Underneath the geopolitics is something every young person feels at the kitchen table: the spread has never felt wider — the cost of living and the monthly rent or mortgage payment on one side, entry-level wages that have stayed stubbornly flat on the other. A roof over your head, renting or owning, shouldn't require winning the lottery.

The Trap

Rent up, wages stuck

When rent eats the paycheck, there's nothing left to save for a down payment — and when rates and prices stay high, owning slips further away. That's not a personal failure. It's a policy outcome — and policy can be changed by people who show up informed.

Education

The roadmap to homeownership

The First Time Homebuyer website exists for exactly this generation: plain-language education, calculators, down-payment help and a step-by-step roadmap so a first home stops being a rumor and becomes a plan — likely qualified options, checked with a licensed loan officer, never promised on a screen.

Opportunity

Curated homes, human help

The FTHB House Finder plugin, powered by the First-Time Homebuyer dashboard's lead-conversion and property-card curation shelf, puts real, curated listing cards in a young buyer's hands — matched, explained, and walked through with a loan officer and a local agent, not an algorithm alone.

For families, for the future: this game was made by a father and husband for his two college-age and recently-graduated kids — and for every young person in their band. The point was never fear. It's kinship: learn together, vote together, build a life together.

The field brief — what the game is teaching

The short version of a long night of research, kept honest: facts where the record is documented, judgment labeled as judgment.

1 · The strait is load-bearing

The Strait of Hormuz normally carries ~20 million barrels of oil a day and about a fifth of global LNG, with only ~2.6 million barrels/day of pipeline bypass. When war came in Feb 2026, prices didn't need a total closure to spike — insurers and shipowners pulling out closed it commercially. U.S. gas went from $2.98 (Feb 28) past $4.50 by May.

2 · Tariffs were already in the prices

New York Fed research put tariffs at +2.9 points of consumer-goods inflation by Feb 2026 — before the first strike. A tariff is a tax collected at the border and largely passed to you. Landed cost = price + freight + insurance + tariff + delay. In 2026, every term in that equation rose at once.

3 · Ask who built the corner

Under the 2015 JCPOA deal, Iran's nuclear “breakout” time was ~12 months, inspected. The U.S. withdrew in May 2018; Iran then escalated in announced steps — stockpile up, enrichment to 60%, inspectors out — until breakout was weeks. That compressed timeline was then cited as the emergency requiring war. The facts were real. The authorship was erased.

4 · The second-order hits

  • Fertilizer: ~⅓ of global shipments transit Hormuz — food prices lag the shock by months.
  • Helium & chips: Gulf-linked helium feeds semiconductor fabs; delays idle whole lines.
  • Rates: the 10-year Treasury pushed past 5.1%, mortgages stayed above ~6.3%, hiring and homebuying froze. Buffers — inventories, spare capacity — are finite and already drawn down.

Price surge — or wage-price spiral? The watch list

  • Temporary surge: headline inflation up, but core and services stay contained, and long-term expectations stay anchored.
  • Spiral warning: core + services inflation accelerate for months, across many categories at once.
  • Unit labor costs: wage growth minus productivity keeps climbing — firms price for expected future costs.
  • Expectations unanchor: 5–10 year inflation expectations stay high even after energy stabilizes.
  • The test that matters: several of these together — not one scary headline.

What the midterms actually control

  • The power of the purse: Congress votes the supplemental war funding and the defense budget. No funding, no blank check.
  • Tariff oversight: Congress can challenge executive tariff authority, force exemptions, and reclaim trade power.
  • War Powers & oversight: resolutions, hearings and subpoenas raise the cost of open-ended escalation.
  • The per-candidate rule: party color alone earns nothing. A candidate who votes for unconditional war funding or tariff escalation hasn't earned your vote — check the record, not just the label.
